verses.text: Another day, God’s sons came to stand before the LORD. Satan came along with them to stand before the LORD too.
The LORD asked Satan, “Where have you come from?” Satan answered, “I’ve been going back and forth across the earth, walking all over it.”

The LORD asked Satan, “Have you taken a look at my servant Job? There’s nobody like him on earth. He’s blameless and upright, he fears God, and he turns away from evil. He’s still holding on to his integrity, even though you stirred me up against him to ruin him for no reason.”
Satan answered the LORD, “Skin for skin. A person will give up everything they own to stay alive.
But reach out your hand and touch his bones and flesh, and he’ll turn his back on you right to your face.”
The LORD told Satan, “All right, he’s in your hands. Just spare his life.”
So Satan left the LORD’s presence and struck Job with painful sores from the soles of his feet to the top of his head.
Job found a piece of broken pottery to scrape his skin with and sat there among the ashes.
His wife said, “Are you still holding on to your integrity? Turn your back on God and die.”
He told her, “You’re talking like one of the foolish women. What, should we take good from God’s hand and refuse trouble?” Through all this, Job didn’t sin in what he said.

When Job’s three friends heard about all the trouble that had come on him, they each came from home: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. They arranged to go together to share his grief and comfort him.
When they looked up from a distance, they didn’t recognize him. They cried out and wept. Each tore his robe and tossed dust over his head toward the sky.
They sat with him on the ground for seven days and seven nights. Nobody said a word to him, because they could see how deep his grief was.
